claim: A kill bit set in the Edward's Castle aqueduct (scenes $0C-$12, numbers $01-$45) is still set when the Inca Ruins load, because the story chain from the aqueduct exit to the Inca Ruins has no ClearAllWramFlags: the aqueduct exit $13 warps to $0A (edward_castle), ec0A_kara.asm:195 queues $06 (wills_house), sc06_kara_return.asm:153 queues $15 (itory_village), the warp $15 -> $17, it17_lily.asm:35 queues $1A, it1A_lily.asm:124 queues $1C (incan_ruins_entrance), warp $1C -> $1D. InitActorFromSceneData then frees every Inca Ruins spawn record whose number matches (ir1D_mudpit rows #06-#0A carry $01-$05, ir1D_four_way $06-$0F, and so on) and the enemy is missing from the scene.

start.state: kill bits $0A80-$0A9F zero (new game or just after a world-map visit); player in the aqueduct entrance scene $0C

trial.control: kill the first bat of scene $0C (row #02, number $01) and read $0A80 (bit 1 must be set); play the story chain without opening the world map until scene $1D loads
trial.forced: poke $0A80 := $01 in scene $1D before the load (or after a warp into $1D) and compare enemiesRemaining ($0AEC) and the actor list with a run where the byte is zero: row #06 (ir1D_mudpit, number $01) must be absent when the bit is set
observe: $0AEC and the visible enemies of scene $1D
whether any ClearAllWramFlags / game-over clear ran between the scenes (breakpoint on 46284 / 54988)

confirms: the bit is still set on entering $1D and the matching Inca Ruins enemy does not spawn
refutes: the byte is zero when $1D loads (an unseen reset), or the enemy spawns despite the bit

claim: Kill bits set in the Pyramid (numbers $01-$FE, notably $01-$05 of pyramid_main and the first rooms) are still set when the Babel dark-lair scenes $F2-$F6 load: the chain pyramid puzzle_room $CD -> $C8 (pyCD_kara.asm:122), warp $C8 -> $C3 (dao), daC3_babel_travel_spirit.asm:62 -> $E3, warps $E3 -> $E2 -> $E0 -> $F2-$F5 and $E3 -> $F6 has no ClearAllWramFlags. The dark-lair boss rows carry the numbers $01-$05 (btF2_neo_castoth $01, btF3_neo_viper $02, btF4 male and female vampire $03, btF5_neo_fanger $04, btF6_neo_queen $05); a stale bit frees the boss record at the load.

start.state: kill bits zero on Pyramid entry; kill the pyramid_main mystic balls (rows #04, #05, numbers $01 and $02) and a first-room enemy with number $03-$05

trial.control: after the kills read $0A80; follow the story to the Babel dark lairs without the world map; read $0A80 before each lair loads
trial.forced: poke $0A80 bits 1-5 before entering scene $F2 and check which boss rows spawn (F2 row #03, F3 #03, F4 #03 and #04, F5 #03, F6 #07)
observe: any clear of the block between the pyramid and Babel

confirms: the bits are still set in the lairs and the matching boss rows are skipped
refutes: the byte is zero on load or the boss spawns with the bit set (an unseen guard)

claim: On the sp58 path with $0AA6 = 1 the Sky Garden kill bits survive into Mu: sp58_monologue (sp58_monologue.asm, QueueMapChange #5A at {426974}) leaves scene $58 for $5A without a reset, while the reset in sp58_red_eye (ClearAllWramFlags {426502}) runs only when $0AA6 = 2 ({426392}-{426398}). Warp $5A -> $5E -> $5F then loads Mu; 57 enemy numbers occur in both the Sky Garden scenes ($4D-$54) and the Mu scenes ($5F-$65).

start.state: Sky Garden finished with $0AA6 = 1; kill bits of the garden set

trial.control: read $0AA6 when scene $58 loads, kill-bit bytes before and after leaving $58, and again when Mu ($5F) loads
trial.forced: poke $0AA6 := 2 in scene $58 to see the reset run (control for the other branch)

confirms: the bytes are unchanged between $58 and $5F on the $0AA6 = 1 path and the matching Mu enemies are absent
refutes: the bytes are zero on $5F, or $0AA6 is always 2 at this point

claim: awB1_wall_walker rows (66 numbers) may never write their kill bit: the actor ORs the boss bit $0080 into extendedFlags at {769087} and {769211}, and StandardEnemyDefeatHandler skips SetDungeonKillFlag when that bit is set ({56301}); the own death routine code_0BC11B sets the bit ({770381}) for every non-last kill, and the last kill (enemiesRemaining = 1) goes through the standard handler. Which kills reach which branch is not traced.

start.state: Angkor Wat scene $B1 freshly entered; $0A80-$0A9F zero

trial.control: kill a wall walker that is not the last enemy and read the bit of its number (row #05 of $B1 is number $13: byte $0A82 bit 3)
trial.forced: kill the last enemy of the scene as a wall walker and read the bit again
observe: bit of the number after each kill

confirms: non-last kills set the bit, the last kill sets it only without the boss bit
refutes: no bit is set, or every kill sets it

claim: pyD2_haunt rows may never write their kill bit: OrExtraFlags #$0090 ({770788}) includes the boss bit, so StandardEnemyDefeatHandler (which the actor reaches by JumpFar) skips SetDungeonKillFlag; when the OrExtraFlags runs relative to the death is not traced.

start.state: Pyramid haunt room freshly entered, $0A80-$0A9F zero

trial.control: kill a haunt and read the bit of its number

claim: awB0_zombie rows never write their kill bit: SetDeathCallback code_0BB800 ({767902}, body {768000}-{768022}) stores 1 at offset $26 of the actor addressed by DP $26, plays the sound and spawns EnemyDeathFlash, and the file has no SetDungeonKillFlag, StandardEnemyDefeatHandler, EnemyDefeatDispatch or Die; what the callback's return leads to (and whether enemiesRemaining is ever decremented) is not resolved.

start.state: Angkor Wat scene $B0 freshly entered, $0A80-$0A9F zero

trial.control: defeat a zombie (row of number $09) and read $0A81 bit 1, enemiesRemaining and whether the actor stays

confirms: no bit is set and the counter does not change

claim: ec12_skull_chaser (numbers $44 and $45) sets its kill bit on the second death only: the first death runs the callback code_0A853E ({689282}), which resets the stats and clears the callback ({689513}); the second death takes the default routing.

trial.control: kill a skull chaser once and read $0A88 bits 4 and 5; kill it again and read them again
observe: the actor state between the deaths

confirms: the bit is clear after the first death and set after the second
refutes: the bit is set after the first death

claim: The dark-lair fanger (scene $F5 row #03, number $04) never writes its kill bit: gw8A_sand_fanger ORs the boss bit at {756183}, so StandardEnemyDefeatHandler skips SetDungeonKillFlag; the actor files of the neighbouring boss rows (ir29_castoth, sg55_viper, mu67_vampires, pyDD_mummy_queen) contain no OrExtraFlags #$0080, so their rows reach the write.

start.state: dark fanger lair entered, bit 4 of $0A80 clear

trial.control: defeat the fanger and read $0A80 bit 4

claim: The Great Wall tomb Dark Space actor (gw88_tomb_dark_space.asm:18 {507380}) fires its background change and sets event flag $0174 when the six stone archers of scene $88 (rows #0C-#11, numbers $F8-$FD) are all dead: LDA $0A9F, AND #$00FF, CMP #$003F means bits 0-5 set ($F8-$FD) and bits 6-7 clear ($FE, $FF).

start.state: scene $88 freshly entered from the world map (kill bits zero); event flag $0174 clear

trial.control: kill the six stone archers one by one and read $0A9F after each; watch for the background change
trial.forced: poke $0A9F := $3F in the scene and check that the change fires; poke $0A9F := $7F (bit of $FE set) and check that it does not

confirms: the change fires exactly when the low byte of $0A9F reads $3F
refutes: the change fires with another value, or never fires
